# 🔮 Add Allora Network Connection

## Overview
This PR adds support for the Allora Network, enabling agents to fetch and utilize network inferences for various topics. The integration allows seamless access to Allora's predictive capabilities through a standardized connection interface.

## Features
- New `AlloraConnection` class implementing the `BaseConnection` interface
- Support for Allora API authentication and configuration
- Two primary actions:
  - `get-inference`: Fetch network inference for specific topics
  - `list-topics`: Retrieve available Allora Network topics
- Chain slug configuration with default testnet support
- Environment-based API key management

1. **API Key Setup**
   - Set the `ALLORA_API_KEY` in your `.env` file
   - To generate the API key, use the [Upshot Developer Portal](https://developer.upshot.xyz/signup)

2. **Basic Connection Test**
   ```bash
   configure-connection allora
   list-connections  # Verify Allora shows as configured
   ```

3. **Testing Inference Retrieval**
   ```bash
   # Direct action testing
   agent-action allora get-inference 1
   > Result: {'topic_id': 1, 'inference': '3671.388101940282107932'}

title: Rework timestamp utilization for timezone consistency
body:
## Describe changes
Following the previous PR (https://github.com/zenml-io/zenml/pull/3265) that replaced deprecated `datetime.utcnow()` with `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, some follow-up is required to ensure we use timezone-aware timestamps appropriately:

1. no timezone aware timestamps must be stored in the database. The convention is that the database stores only timezone-naive UTC timestamps 
2. comparisons and subtraction operations between timezone-aware and timezone-naive operands result in errors, so they must be avoided

This PR introduces a few time utils to make it easier to deal with timezones. It also goes through all occurrences of `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` and re-evaluates whether a timezone-aware timestamp is indeed needed and reverts some of the decisions in the previous PR if that's not the case.

title: fix(flags): Fix bug where concurrent accesses to the flags property could raise a RunTime error
body:
On error the SDK deep copies the flag buffer. If the SDK is receiving flags at the same time, the buffer copy can potentially raise a RunTime error.  To fix this we guard the FlagBuffer with a lock.

Fixes: https://sentry.sentry.io/issues/6286673308/?project=1

title: [CUDA] Preload dependent DLLs
body:
### Description

Changes:
(1) Pass --cuda_version in packaging pipeline to build wheel command line so that cuda_version can be saved. Note that cuda_version is also required for generating extra_require for https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/pull/23659.
(2) Update steup.py and onnxruntime_validation.py to save cuda version to capi/build_and_package_info.py.
(3) Add a helper function to preload dependent DLLs (MSVC, CUDA, CUDNN) in `__init__.py`. First we will try to load DLLs from nvidia site packages, then try load remaining DLLs with default path settings.

```
import onnxruntime
onnxruntime.preload_dlls()
```

To show loaded DLLs, set `verbose=True`. It is also possible to disable loading some types of DLLs like:
```
onnxruntime.preload_dlls(cuda=False, cudnn=False, msvc=False, verbose=True)
```

#### PyTorch and onnxruntime in Windows

When working with pytorch,  onnxruntime will reuse the CUDA and cuDNN DLLs loaded by pytorch as long as CUDA and cuDNN major versions are compatible. Preload DLLs actually might cause issues (see example 2 and 3 below) in Windows.

Example 1: onnxruntime and torch can work together easily. 
```
>>> import torch
>>> import onnxruntime
>>> session = onnxruntime.InferenceSession("model.onnx", providers=["CUDAExecutionProvider"])
>>> onnxruntime.preload_dlls(cuda=False, cudnn=False, msvc=False, verbose=True)
----List of loaded DLLs----
D:\anaconda3\envs\py310\Lib\site-packages\torch\lib\curand64_10.dll
D:\anaconda3\envs\py310\Lib\site-packages\torch\lib\cufft64_11.dll

Previously, when autorun on startup was disabled, running a cell wouldn't transition it out of stale. For long-running cells, this would give the incorrect impression to the user that their cell had not been submitted for execution.

This change updates the kernel to register uninstantiated cells as stale, so they are correctly transitioned out of stale on run.

title: Client HTTP Module Refactoring and Test Fixes
body:
## Overview
This PR introduces a new HTTP client architecture for the AgentOps SDK and fixes related tests. The architecture follows a clean separation of concerns design principle, making the code more maintainable, testable, and extensible.

## New Architecture

### Components

#### HttpClient
- Provides low-level HTTP functionality with connection pooling and retry logic
- Manages session creation and reuse
- Offers both regular and authenticated sessions
- Implements basic HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)

#### AuthManager
- Handles authentication concerns including token acquisition, storage, and refresh
- Provides thread-safe token operations
- Prepares authentication headers for requests
- Detects expired tokens from API responses

#### HTTP Adapters
- **BaseHTTPAdapter**: Enhanced connection pooling and retry logic
- **AuthenticatedHttpAdapter**: Extends BaseHTTPAdapter with authentication capabilities, automatically refreshing tokens when needed

#### Exporters
- **AuthenticatedOTLPExporter**: OpenTelemetry exporter with authentication support

### Design Principles
1. **Separation of Concerns**: HTTP concerns are isolated from authentication concerns
2. **Composition over Inheritance**: Components use composition rather than inheritance
3. **Clear Interfaces**: Each component has a well-defined interface
4. **Dependency Flow**: Dependencies flow in one direction


## Benefits
1. **Improved Testability**: Each component can be tested in isolation
2. **Better Error Handling**: Clear separation of authentication and HTTP errors
3. **Enhanced Maintainability**: Single responsibility principle applied throughout
4. **Extensibility**: New authentication methods or HTTP features can be added without affecting existing code
reason: The PR introduces a new HTTP client architecture and improves the design and testability of the code without fixing a bug or adding a new feature from the user's perspective. It is primarily a refactor to improve code structure and maintainability.

title: fix(weave): Fixing filtering calls table by boolean
body:
## Description

- Fixes WB-23754

We use a `LIKE` optimization for "heavy" conditions. The `LIKE` condition template wraps the literal value in double quotes, which is good for strings, but boolean literals are not wrapped in quotes in JSON payloads.

One corner case of this fix is that when filtering by strings `"true"` or `"false"` (not the boolean), the optimization may also match any call with strings containing those substrings (e.g. `"trued"`). This is not a concern as the final filtering would remove those (tested). It just makes the optimization slightly less optimal in those rare corner cases.

## Testing

How was this PR tested?

- tested manually with boolean values and string values `"true"`.
- modified the `test_query_heavy_column_simple_filter_with_order_and_limit_and_mixed_query_conditions` unit test to cover the boolean case.

title: fix(providers): add logging and fix custom python provider caching
body:
Custom Python providers were not always caching responses. The below example shows a provider where caching fails:

```
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel
from openai import OpenAI


OPENAI_CLIENT = OpenAI()


class Poem(BaseModel):
    """A funny poem."""

    poem: str


# The following classes are needed for promptfoo
class ProviderOptions:
    id: str | None
    config: dict[str, Any] | None


class CallApiContextParams:
    vars: dict[str, str]


class TokenUsage(BaseModel):
    total: int
    prompt: int
    completion: int


class ProviderResponse(BaseModel):
    output: list[str] | str| None
    error: str | None = None
    tokenUsage: TokenUsage | None = None
    cost: float | None = None
    cached: bool | None = None
    logProbs: list[float] | None = None


# Default function called by Promptfoo
def call_api(prompt: str, options: dict[str, Any], context: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    config = options.get("config", None)
    llm_model = config.get("llm_model", "gpt-4o")

    response = OPENAI_CLIENT.beta.chat.completions.parse(
        model=llm_model,
        messages=[
            {
                "role": "user",
                "content": prompt,
            }
        ],
        response_format=Poem,
    )
    poem = response.choices[0].message.parsed.poem
    return ProviderResponse(output=poem).model_dump()
```

Run with this config:

```
description: Write poems

prompts:
  - "Write a funny poem about {topic}"

providers:
  - file://providers/poem.py

tests:
  - vars:
      topic: "a cat"
  - vars:
      topic: "a dog"
  - vars:
      topic: "cakes"
  - vars:
      topic: "a computer"
```

title: Fixing Smart Wallet with Solana Keypair admin signer issues
body: # Relates to: Smart Wallet with Solana Keypair admin signer # Background In some transactions, we were encountering issues with: Missing signature: where the transaction would fail because the signer was not properly attached Too many signatures: where additional_signers were being appended multiple times, causing redundant signatures. ## What does this PR do? This PR improves the transaction signing flow by: - Updating `send_transaction()` to fallback to `self._admin_signer` if no signer is provided in the transaction payload. - Cleaning up `send_raw_transaction()` to prevent duplication in the signers list by ensuring `additional_signers` are only appended once. These changes ensure the correct signer is always present and that transactions include the required, but only necessary, signatures — resolving both the missing and excessive signature issues. # Testing ## Detailed testing results | Method | Prompt | Screenshot | Transaction Link | |----------|--------|-------|------------------| |transfer_native | send 0.001 sol to HfP9zRYy2y7kZto4fuNiNJ3F9gkEkW5P4XnEpDWeMCtU | |https://solscan.io/tx/64KSrt1efueSwwb3DbqrDYq6iKM39KnYjMycX3TSKDgLJXhTqegR1YT8PXjzLXUGGn6SGk67MZTU5veGVPdYYaMD?cluster=devnet | transfer_native is defined as follows : ``` def transfer_native(self,recipient: str, amount_lamports: int) -> None: wallet = self._wallet_client #where wallet_client is `SolanaSmartWalletClient` with keypair admin signer print("\n💸 Preparing transaction...") instructions = [transfer(TransferParams(from_pubkey=Pubkey.from_string(wallet.get_address()), to_pubkey=Pubkey.from_string(recipient), lamports=amount_lamports))] print(f"📝 Transaction Details:") print(f" From: {wallet.get_address()}") print(f" To: {recipient}") print(f" Amount: {amount_lamports} lamports") print("\n📤 Sending transaction to network...") transaction_response = wallet.send_transaction( { "instructions": instructions, } ) print(f"✅ Transaction sent successfully!") print(f"🔗 Transaction Hash: {transaction_response.get('hash')}") return transaction_response ``` # Docs ## Checklist - [✅ ] I have tested this change and added the relevant screenshots to the PR description - [ ✅] I updated the [README](https://github.com/goat-sdk/goat/blob/main/README.md) if necessary to include the new plugin, wallet, chain, etc. If you require releasing a new version of the package: - [ ] I have added a changset for the specific package by running `pnpm change:add` from the `typescript` directory

title: Feat!: Add support for multiple virtual layers controlled by gateway
body:
This update adds support for managing a virtual layer per gateway, so a `gateway` when specified in the model will be responsible to create the views of the virtual layer as well as the physical tables. This is controlled by setting the provisionally called `gateway_managed_virtual_layer` flag to true in the config.

```yaml
gateways:
  local:
    connection:
      type: postgres
      ...

  bigquery_gw:
    connection:
      type: bigquery
    variables:
      overriden_var: 'bigquery'

  snowflake_gw:
    connection:
      type: snowflake
      database: db1
      ...
    variables:
      overriden_var: 'snowflake'

default_gateway: postgres

gateway_managed_virtual_layer: true
```

In this case the virtual layer will be created by the specific gateway instead of using the default gateway, which means that the catalog doesn't need to be shared between the gateways. Also the gateway specific catalog will be set for each corresponding model and the gateway specific variables will take precedence over global ones for the gateway-specified in the model.

The default behaviour remains unchanged when the flag is set to false or omitted from the config.
reason: The PR introduces a new feature that allows managing multiple virtual layers controlled by different gateways, which is a new capability added to the system.

title: feat: Enhance memory system with isolated memory configuration
body:
This PR introduces several improvements to the memory system:

1. Support for isolated memory configuration
   - Users can now define individual memory types independently. This change makes it easier to use a specific memory type without unintentionally enabling all others. Previously, setting memory=True would implicitly configure all available memories (like LTM and STM), which might not be ideal in all cases. 
   For example, when building a chatbot that only needs an external memory, users were forced to also configure LTM and STM — which rely on default OpenAPI embeddings — even if they weren’t needed. 
   With this update, users can now define a single memory in isolation, making the configuration process simpler and more flexible.

2. Enhanced memory documentation
   - Improved documentation for memory system usage and configuration
   - Better clarity on memory types and their interactions

3. Warning system for memory configuration
   - Added warning when long-term memory is enabled without entity memory
   - Helps users avoid potential memory configuration issues

title: More flexible TrainableModel
body:
This PR makes a few changes to the API shape, specifically focused on `Model` and `LocalAPI`.

It introduces an abstraction where we separate out `PolicyModel`, which could be any LLM, and a `TrainablePolicyModel`, which is specifically a policy that can be trained by our system. This will let us log trajectories from both `PolicyModel` and `TrainablePolicyModel` in a unified way.

It also adds a new `config` field to `PolicyModel`. This is opaque to our system, but is something we can log to wandb and our file system in the future to track hparams associated with each model run. I'm using the config field in the following way:

```python
agent_002 = art.TrainablePolicyModel(
    name="email-agent-002",
    project="email_agent",
    base_model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct",
    config=ProjectPolicyConfig(
        max_turns=10,
        training_config=TrainingConfig(
            trajectories_per_group=6,
            groups_per_step=1,
            learning_rate=1.2e-5,
            eval_steps=30,
            val_set_size=100,
            training_dataset_size=4000,
            batch_size=8,
            num_epochs=4,
        ),
    ),
)

agent_004 = agent_002.model_copy(deep=True)
assert isinstance(agent_004.config, ProjectPolicyConfig)
agent_004.name = "email-agent-004"
agent_004.config.max_turns = 30
```

And then within my training and rollout functions, adjusting behavior based on the config above. I find this pattern helps me stay sane by tracking what properties each model was called with, and keeping a record around of old training runs (by keeping the old config in the codebase).
reason: The PR introduces a new abstraction and adds a new configuration field to the existing API, which enhances the functionality and flexibility of the TrainableModel. These changes add new features rather than fixing bugs or refactoring existing code.

title: fix: Remove kwargs from all RagTools
body:
Closes https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI/issues/2685

The agent uses the tool description to decide what to propagate when a tool with **kwargs is found, but this often leads to failures during the tool invocation step.

This happens because the final description ends up like this:

```
CrewStructuredTool(name='Knowledge base', description='Tool Name: Knowledge base
Tool Arguments: {'query': {'description': None, 'type': 'str'}, 'kwargs': {'description': None, 'type': 'Any'}}
Tool Description: A knowledge base that can be used to answer questions.')
```

The agent then tries to infer and pass a kwargs parameter, which isn’t supported by the schema at all.

## Addressed issues

- Remove **kwargs from most RagTool classes: this should help the Agent make better decisions when calling a search Tool.
- Ensure proper configuration when using add: according to the documentation, some search methods must be defined as either a loader or a data_type. This commit ensures that.
- Fix GitHubSearch integration: the current integration was not working properly.
- Tests were added for search tools

title: Fix test_update_returns_state to flatten Kalman output
body:
# Pull Request

## Purpose

Fix `test_update_returns_state` in `test_simple_kalman.py` where the test was incorrectly comparing a 1D list to a 2D list.

The original test:
```python
  def update_returns_state(self):
    x = self.kf.update(100)
    assert x == self.kf.x
```
The test did not had the `test_` prefix so it was never called.
incorrectly assumed that `x` (a 1D list) and `self.kf.x` (a 2D list) were directly comparable.  
This change adds `test_update_returns_state` to the set of tests and explicitly flattens `self.kf.x` during the assertion:
```python
  def test_update_returns_state(self):
    x = self.kf.update(100)
   assert x == [i[0] for i in self.kf.x]
```
This ensures a proper value comparison and prevents false test failures.

---

## Justification

- **Verification**: After this change, the tests pass without modifying the Kalman filter's internal representation.
- **Purpose**: To fix the test structure without altering code functionality.
- **Impact**: Minimal; strictly testing fix, no effect on runtime behavior or functionality.

---

- Confirmed that the test is passing.
- No regressions observed.

title: pytest improvements to handle flaky test
body:
We're facing some flaky tests, including occasional CI timeouts.

This PR doesn’t address all flakiness but introduces some packages to help simulate more deterministic behavior in the future. 

The flakiness issues addressed were:

**fix: prevent crash when event handler raises exception** 
> Previously, if a registered event handler raised an exception during execution,
it could crash the entire application or interrupt the event dispatch process.
This change wraps handler execution in a try/except block within the `emit` method,
ensuring that exceptions are caught and logged without affecting other handlers or flow.
This improves the resilience of the event bus, especially when handling third-party
or temporary listeners.

**test: fix flaky test ValueError: Circular reference detected**
> We need to be cautious when assigning values in the test file, as doing so makes them available in the entire module. For this case, we were facing a circular reference issue when copying Agent instances.. after debugging I noticed that the GC was detecting many Agent attributes twice. To handle it properly within tests I used pytest.fixture for a better scope control


There is another one that I would able to find the root cause, something is causing `ConnectionError`

Implements [Protected Resource Metadata](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc9728/) in mcp-engine.

This RFC essentially requires a new (well known) endpoint located at ".well-known/oauth-protected-resource", which gives metadata about auth related items (such as the authorization servers the client should reach out to).

This PR implements support by:
- Exposing this new endpoint
- Returning the address of this endpoint 401 and 403 responses, within the `WWW-Authenticate` header.

title: Easily track span duration within rollouts
body:
I ran into an issue on my current project where the llm-as-judge I was using was taking a super long time to return, bottlenecking the whole rollout process and leading to low GPU utilization.

This change makes it easy to track the duration of different parts of your rollout with a context manager. For example, to track how long an LLM-as-judge contained within a function takes, you could do the following:

```python
async with traj.track_duration("determine_if_answer_is_correct"):
    rubric.answer_correct = await determine_if_answer_is_correct(
        final_answer, scenario
    )
```

This will automatically add a new metric, `determine_if_answer_is_correct_duration`, which tracks the cumulative duration (in seconds) spent within the context manager.

I also add a new optional method to trajectories, `.finish()` When called, this will add a metric `duration` that tracks the total trajectory duration from start to finish.

Separately, this PR makes it explicit that metrics can be boolean or ints. This mostly already worked bc python will accept `int` in most places that expect `float`, and `bool` is a subclass of `int` in Python (!), but adding it to the types makes it more obvious.

Also fixes a minor type error in the art-e example. We should probably enable automatic typechecking as part of PRs at some point.
reason: The PR introduces a new feature that allows tracking the duration of different parts of a rollout process using a context manager and adds new metrics for duration tracking.

title: feat: support to set an empty context to the Task
body:
Closes #2789

TD;LR

Treat 'falsy' issue while setting context to a Task

----

Currently, the `Task.context` is other tasks whose outputs will be used as context for the task. The default value is None which is a 'falsy' Python value. 
For a Crew `None` means: get the context from all previous tasks outputs. This creates a limitation, because we currently have no way to explicitly say, “this task should have no additional context.

This PR address this issue by allowing us to set empty value in a Task's context. From now on, any falsy Python value (like `None`, `[]`, or `False`) will be treated as "no context should be used" for the task
reason: The PR introduces a new feature that allows setting an empty context to a Task, changing how falsy values are treated for task context.

title: Implement concurrent.futures instrumentation for OpenTelemetry contex…
body:
## 📥 Pull Request

**📘 Description**
While implementing mem0 instrumentation, discovered that multiple isolated traces were being created instead of proper parent-child span relationships within a session. This broke the trace hierarchy and made it difficult to understand the flow of operations.

Root Cause: mem0 (and potentially other LLM libraries) uses `ThreadPoolExecutor` for concurrent operations, but AgentOps lacked instrumentation for thread pool execution contexts. This caused trace context to be lost when operations moved to background threads, resulting in orphaned spans instead of a cohesive trace tree.

- Added a new module for instrumenting the concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor to ensure proper OpenTelemetry context propagation across threads.
- Introduced the ConcurrentFuturesInstrumentor class, which wraps the ThreadPoolExecutor's initialization and submission methods to maintain context.
- Enhanced the _should_instrument_package function to include utility instrumentors in the instrumentation decision process.
- Updated the TARGET_PACKAGES set to include utility instrumentors for comprehensive monitoring.
- Added unit tests to validate context propagation behavior in concurrent execution scenarios, ensuring spans share trace IDs correctly across threads.

These changes improve the observability and reliability of concurrent operations within the AgentOps SDK.

**🧪 Testing**

title: Fix tracing disablement conflict between predict_fn and scorers
body:
🛠 DevTools 🛠

[![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/B-Step62/mlflow/pull/16103?quickstart=1) #### Install mlflow from this PR ``` # mlflow pip install git+https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow.git@refs/pull/16103/merge # mlflow-skinny pip install git+https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow.git@refs/pull/16103/merge#subdirectory=skinny ``` For Databricks, use the following command: ``` %sh curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mlflow/mlflow/HEAD/dev/install-skinny.sh | sh -s pull/16103/merge ```

### What changes are proposed in this pull request? #### Problem https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/pull/16004 added `@trace_disabled` tag to scorers execution. This was for making sure custom scorers do not generate traces in evaluation run. Currently, the evaluation result page simply show all traces in the Run, so having such extra traces breaks the result and metric aggregation. However, the above change caused a thread-safety problem. In evaluation harness, model prediction and scorer execution is done concurrently in a thread pool for performance optimization. Trace disabling is global, not thread local, so the above disablement logic sometimes causes side effect that predict_fn does not generate traces. This is a regression. #### Short-term Solution (this PR) Unfortunately, disabling tracing in thread-local way is quite challenging. Therefore, we take the following approach as a short-term fix. 1. Just let traces generated from scorers. 2. Once evaluation harness completes, run `mlflow.search_traces()` to get traces in the evaluation run. 3. Traces generated from predict function always have `eval.requestId` tag. Therefore, we can determine extra traces by checking the existence of this tag. 4. Delete these extra traces by calling `mlflow.delete_traces()`. #### Long-term Solution From product perspective, we should actually allow those extra traces to be generated. For example, users may want to check the OpenAI LLM call inside their LLM-as-a-Judge scorers. Therefore, the fundamental problem is how we display evaluation results. It should not just show all traces in the run, but instead filter them by certain criteria e.g. if the trace has assessment created by the evaluation. Post-DAIS, we will change how traces are associated with Run and how evaluation result page fetches list of traces to show. After that change, we should be able to remove this hack. ### How is this PR tested? - [x] Existing unit/integration tests - [x] New unit/integration tests - [x] Manual tests ``` import json import mlflow from mlflow.genai.scorers import scorer, Correctness from mlflow.entities import AssessmentSource, Feedback mlflow.openai.autolog() @scorer def harmfulness(outputs) -> Feedback: import openai prompt = f''' Judge if the following text is harmful or not. title: Add support for tag-based component filtering
body:
## Add Tag-Based Component Filtering

This PR introduces tag-based filtering for FastMCP components (tools, resources, resource templates, and prompts), allowing servers to selectively expose functionality based on configurable include/exclude tag sets.

### Key Features
- **Include Tags**: Only components with matching tags are exposed
- **Exclude Tags**: Components with matching tags are filtered out  
- **Precedence**: Exclude tags take priority over include tags
- **Universal Support**: Works across all component types (tools, resources, templates, prompts)

### Usage
```python
# Only expose components tagged with "public" or "api"
mcp = FastMCP(include_tags={"public", "api"})

# Hide components tagged as "internal" or "deprecated" 
mcp = FastMCP(exclude_tags={"internal", "deprecated"})

@mcp.tool(tags={"public", "utility"})
def my_tool(): ...
```

### Implementation
- Added `include_tags` and `exclude_tags` parameters to `FastMCP` constructor and `Settings`
- Implemented `_should_enable_component()` method with comprehensive filtering logic
- Updated all MCP protocol handlers to respect tag filters
- Added `tags` parameter to component decorators (`@tool`, `@resource`, `@prompt`)

Comprehensive test coverage included for all scenarios and edge cases.

title: [rollout] feat: Support Multi-stage Awake for SGLang
body:
Co-authored with: MrAta (immrata@gmail.com) and @zhaochenyang20 

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PR(s).

### What does this PR do?

### Motivation

In RL Ecosystem which use colocate design like [verl](https://github.com/volcengine/verl/tree/main), we need to offload training model and load serving model & KV Cache frequently.


#### Background
- Currently SGLang is using [torch_memory_saver](https://github.com/fzyzcjy/torch_memory_saver) to pause and resume.
- [torch_memory_saver](https://github.com/fzyzcjy/torch_memory_saver) is a open source repo that provided easy to use api to hack **cudaMalloc** and **cudaFree** to make sure the virtual address could be consistent after pause and resume, which is critical to ensure CUDA Graph work.
- CUDA Graph is critical to make sure SGLang runs faster in decoding phases.


#### Here is the current behavior of VERL + SGLang

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e87e7dd6-f223-4de6-8f07-915eb2030ea8)

1. During Training, we have training model and optimizer state in the GPU Memory, and once training is done, we will offload optimizer state to cpu and keep the model weights in GPU, which is needed in Update Weight.
2. During Update Weight, we awake the SGLang engine, so those paused memory of Model Weights and KV Cache will come back. Then we update model from training model to serving model on the fly using the api: `update_weights_in_tensor`
3. After Model being updated, we delete the training model from GPU Memory.


Above design works pretty well so far, however, this would waste a big chunk of GPU Memory during rollout, which could cause a few issues we've seen so far:
- **Small KV Cache**: We need to use relative lower number of mem fraction ratio (e.g: 0.6), hence our KV Cache has less tokens. Given KV Cache has less tokens, we will hit `RuntimeError: Prefill out of memory. Try to lower your batch size.` when we try prefill large number of requests.
- **Out of Memory**: If we use mem fraction ratio 0.8 and run RL for 32B model on 8 H100, it will OOM during update weight


#### Challenge
- `torch_memory_saver` currently only supports Singleton, hence SGLang will pause and resume KV Cache + Weights together, they are treated as the same group of memory controlled by the singleton `torch_memory_saver` instance

#### Proposal
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fda9638-0dc2-4c14-bc64-cd20616f350f)

1. During Training, we do the same
2. During Update Weight Stage 1, we awake the model weights from SGLang and then update weights
3. During Update Weight Stage 2, we delete the training model weights from GPU Memory
4. Awake the SGLang's KV Cache


![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3dab327-dc2e-4ed8-88d7-15e383f77d25)


### Benefit
With above feature, we can train larger model with same GPU, we can also make training/rollout more efficient given we can allocate larger KV Cache

### Solution: Keep using Singleton and provide tag based pause/resume

- [x] Support tag based resume/pause: https://github.com/fzyzcjy/torch_memory_saver/pull/20
- [x] Support Multiple Stage Awake in SGLang: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/7099
- [ ] Support Multiple Stage Awake in verl: https://github.com/volcengine/verl/pull/1911

title: Improve JupyterLab extension build time
body:
This PR reduces the build time of the JupyterLab package from ~70s/30s/30s (on Windows/Ubuntu/Mac) to ~15s/10s/13s by eliminating the heavyweight `jupyterlab` dependency. Instead, we build and bundle the JavaScript + Python directly using the `@jupyter/builder` npm package. 

Additionally, we get rid of `jlpm` (a.k.a. yarn) in favor of using `npm` which we already use in the rest of our build.

The `jupyterlab-core` dir contains the minimal configuration, that `@jupyter/builder` uses, that previously lived in the `jupyterlab` package. This is really all we needed from there.
 
The resulting packages should be identical.

I've ruled out:
- eliminating the webpack dependency in favor of a different bundler, since the JupyterLab extension architecture uses webpack module federation - there's no getting rid of it.
- removing the JupyterLab package completely - this feels very heavyhanded to me, considering how minimal the build now is and how we still get value from the package IMO (Q# syntax highlighting). 
- checking in the built files - the built files are webpack-bundled, and not very readable. Checking in these artifacts directly would again be pretty heavy-handed, sacrificing maintainability to save a few seconds of build time.

Fixes #2482
reason: The PR introduces a new build approach that significantly improves the build time of the JupyterLab extension, which is a performance enhancement rather than a bug fix or new feature.

body:
## Description

From what I can tell, `traverse_sdfg_with_defined_symbols()` is supposed to traverse the SDFG, accumulating symbols as it runs down the tree. The current implementation resets the dict of "already known symbols" when recursing down into a state that is the source of an edge. That seems odd. In particular, not even the globally available `sdfg.symbols` are marked as defined anymore with that reset.

The proposed fix passes along already known symbols like in all other cases, ensuring that the dict of known symbols only ever grows.

title: [gemma3n] Correctly scale text embeddings for quantized gemma3n conversions
body:
When quantizing the `Gemma3nTextScaledWordEmbedding` module, it follows this code path:
- https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/2c11d10/python/mlx/nn/layers/embedding.py#L42
- https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/2c11d10/python/mlx/nn/layers/quantized.py#L138

Which ends up overwriting the `Gemma3nTextScaledWordEmbedding` instance with `QuantizedEmbedding`. This means that `Gemma3nTextScaledWordEmbedding.__call__` never gets called when the model is quantized.

Fix this issue by moving the scaling outside of `Gemma3nTextScaledWordEmbedding` and deleting `Gemma3nTextScaledWordEmbedding`.

@awni : I would be curious to hear your thoughts on how to enable the use case of inheriting from `nn.Embeddings` while correctly quantizing the underlying weights in the base class.
reason: The change fixes an issue where the text embeddings were not correctly scaled during quantization, which is a bug fix in the quantization process of the Gemma3nTextScaledWordEmbedding module.
